incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion claimed by the 'Gentlemen' group, which accessed parts of the IT environment and threatens to leak stolen data.
incidents.impact: Australia's second-largest sugar producer had two mills (Racecourse and Farleigh) shut since June 10, halting harvesting across Queensland's Mackay region; restoration is ongoing.

incidents.vector: Threat actor 'TeamPCP' (tied to the Shai-Hulud worm) compromises maintainer credentials and CI/CD pipelines to inject credential-stealing malware into packages, which then propagates to downstream users.
incidents.impact: Over 1,000 packages compromised since February (≈500M combined weekly downloads); claimed victims include Red Hat, GitHub, Mercor, LiteLLM and SAP. Researchers assess the motivation is notoriety and chaos rather than large extortion payouts.

incidents.victim: Consumer Android TV-box owners (1.5M–2.5M daily IPs)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ad fraud / proxy botnet
incidents.vector: The Popa botnet (a Vo1d/Badbox-linked plugin) is bundled into pirated streaming apps and modded TV boxes, enrolling home devices as residential proxies that relay traffic on demand.
incidents.impact: Researchers tied Popa's proxy pool to NASDAQ-listed Israeli firm Alarum Technologies' NetNut service; the botnet relays traffic linked to ad fraud, account takeovers and mass data-scraping across 1.5–2.5M IPs daily.

incidents.attacker: Unknown — ethical researcher, no malicious exploitation
incidents.vector: Client-side-only authorization in FIFA's Microsoft Entra tenant let a self-registered 'football agent' account reach backend APIs with no server-side enforcement.
incidents.impact: An ethical hacker gained control of World Cup broadcast streams, match-management and commentary systems (able to black out or replace live feeds and alter scores) before responsibly reporting via CISA/FBI; FIFA fixed it the next day.

incidents.vector: Takeover of the 'ehindero' npm maintainer account was used to publish 140+ poisoned @mastra packages depending on a malicious dayjs typosquat ('easy-day-js') whose postinstall hook dropped a C2 implant.
incidents.impact: Any developer or CI/CD pipeline running npm install after the compromise risked credential, token and build-environment theft via a detached, persistent tasking client. Packages were removed and attacker publish access revoked.

incidents.vector: A fully automated credential-reuse, credential-stuffing and password-spraying operation validated logins against exposed Fortinet management and VPN interfaces, then used compromised devices as listening posts to harvest more credentials.
incidents.impact: SOCRadar found a verified database of working credentials for 30,791 devices across 194 countries spanning government, telecom, healthcare and critical infrastructure; victim selection was weighted toward NATO members, with a defense-industry VPN among the data.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of FortiSandbox flaws disclosed in April — CVE-2026-39808 (OS command injection) and CVE-2026-39813 (path traversal) — to bypass authentication, escalate privileges and run arbitrary commands.
incidents.impact: Researchers observed ~49 exploitation events from multiple independent operators across nine countries; compromise of these trusted analysis appliances could grant elevated access within security-sensitive environments.

incidents.vector: Malicious USB-delivered .lnk shortcuts deploy a worm and a clipboard 'clipper' that uses Windows Script Host, a bundled Tor proxy and a hidden-service C2 to steal seed phrases and private keys and substitute wallet addresses.
incidents.impact: Active since February 2026, the clipper performs high-frequency clipboard theft, screenshot exfiltration and remote code execution over Tor, functioning as a lightweight backdoor in addition to a stealer.

incidents.vector: Phishing emails carrying fake business documents launch a heavily obfuscated, fileless infection chain that injects Phantom Stealer into the Windows Explorer process.
incidents.impact: The malware-as-a-service stealer harvests browser credentials, session cookies and financial data, exfiltrating via Telegram, Discord, FTP and SMTP; a single banking-endpoint session can expose transfer-system and admin credentials.

incidents.vector: After Microsoft dismantled the Fox Tempest signing service, the 'Lorem Ipsum' operators pivoted to ClickFix lures on compromised WordPress sites, tricking users into pasting a PowerShell command that installs a shellcode loader and backdoor.
incidents.impact: Researchers link the campaign to Rapid Brigantine (aka Vanilla Tempest / Vice Society), a financially motivated group tied to multiple ransomware families, broadening the victim pool to anyone browsing five-plus hijacked sites.

incidents.victim: ShinyHunters extortion victims (Council of Europe, Ralph Lauren, JCPenney, Nexstar, U. of Nottingham)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of an Oracle PeopleSoft ERP zero-day (CVE-2026-35273, missing authentication for a critical function) to steal data, followed by extortion threats on a dark-web leak site.
incidents.impact: A new batch of victims was listed for extortion; the University of Nottingham confirmed theft of 40GB+ affecting 450,000+ students and alumni. CISA added the PeopleSoft flaw to its KEV catalog.

incidents.vector: Attacker abused the AUR 'orphaned package' adoption mechanism to take over 1,900+ abandoned packages and add install steps that pulled a malicious npm package (later a Bun script) delivering a rootkit and infostealer.
incidents.impact: The infostealer harvests browser, Electron-app and developer credentials and access keys; affected users were urged to rotate all secrets and remove rootkit persistence. The attack remained ongoing as defenders responded.

incidents.victim: Awesome Motive WordPress plugin users (1.2M+ sites)
incidents.vector: Malicious code added to legitimate JavaScript in three Awesome Motive plugins (OptinMonster, TrustPulse, PushEngage) waits for an admin login, creates a rogue admin account, then installs a self-hiding backdoor plugin.
incidents.impact: More than 1.2 million websites were backdoored following the developer's compromise, granting attackers persistent administrative access.

incidents.vector: Intruders gained access to parts of the company's internal network; investigation ongoing.
incidents.impact: The Danish pharma giant (maker of Ozempic and Wegovy) took systems offline to evict attackers and confirmed some sensitive data, including patient PII, was copied.

incidents.vector: Attacker allegedly compromised a developer laptop and stole private multisig keys.
incidents.impact: Roughly $36 million in crypto-assets was stolen and the Humanity token lost nearly 90% of its value shortly after the hack.

incidents.vector: Group 'FulcrumSec' stole terabytes of data from an unsecured database exposed online, then leaked it after ransom negotiations failed.
incidents.impact: Stolen data allegedly includes passport details of children and parents, attendance records, teacher passwords and campus-visitor photos across nine countries.

incidents.vector: Data-extortion group 'Shadowbyt3$' claims it stole data from third-party supplier TINYpulse and is demanding a $2 million ransom.
incidents.impact: The group claims roughly 1GB of employee and business data; Nintendo is being extorted with threats to release the information.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack on the firm, which supplies finance-related software to Russian companies and banks.
incidents.impact: Astral attributed a week-long IT outage disrupting business and government services to the attack.

incidents.victim: Iranian banks (Bank Melli, Tejarat, Saderat, Export Development Bank)
incidents.vector: Attack targeting communications infrastructure shared by four of Iran's largest banks.
incidents.impact: Online portals and mobile apps were down over a weekend; the country's banking council said no customer data was accessed.

incidents.vector: Data allegedly stolen from a government agency that manages healthcare entitlements.
incidents.impact: Personal information of more than 67 million Thai citizens was allegedly taken; some appeared on online black markets, prompting a government probe.

incidents.vector: Suspected Russian hackers breached the lawmaker's Signal messaging account; the FBI notified him of the compromise.
incidents.impact: Bacon, a vocal Ukraine supporter and Kremlin critic, had his encrypted-messaging account accessed in an apparent espionage operation.
